text:
maria: FYI CI is red on smallbatch perf after the driver/nvrtc bump, seeing big jitter in KV-prefetch latency. this looks like prefetch threads are hopping CPUs and causing cache thrash.

infra-bot: nightly-ci smallbatch-throughput (job: runtime/smallbatch) failed — median latency x2.1 vs baseline. logs: https://ci.internal/reports/2245678901 · created PERF-4123

ken: can you paste the minimal repro / perf samples? unsure if it's kernel selection or OS scheduling.

maria: quick repro attached, short log and perf sample. root cause looks like prefetch_worker waking on different cores repeatedly. flame: prefetch_worker -> sleep_for -> wake -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> kernel_launch -> prefetch_worker. wakeups/sec jumped from ~20 -> 500.

maria: ```
# perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations -p $PID
# before: context-switches 1.2k, cpu-migrations 2
# after:  context-switches 14.5k, cpu-migrations 482
```

sasha: interesting — driver 552.1.2 release notes mention a scheduler tweak that can change nvrtc worker thread affinity. might be the nvrtc change, not triton or our kernel.

ryan: does the repro run pinned host threads? our prefetch pool uses std::thread detached threads with no explicit affinity. if CUDA/NVRTC starts setting affinity at kernel launch time we can get involuntary migrations. try forcing affinity in the runtime to confirm.

maria: tried a quick env patch: GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY=0-3 REDWOOD_PREFETCH_PIN=1 ./bazel-bin/runtime/test_smallbatch -> prefetch wakeups dropped and latency returned near baseline.

ken: can you bisect nvrtc/driver? suspect nvrtc PR abc1234 changed worker startup flags. open bisect branch and test with driver 551 vs 552.

maria: running bisect now (branch: perf/bisect-prefetch-affinity). first two runs: 551 -> good, 552 -> bad. nvrtc pinned to 11.8.1 (changed in driver 552 bundle).

ci-bot: triggered perf job perf/bisect-prefetch-affinity on k8s-ci-20 (2 runs queued).

sasha: short-term options: 1) rollback driver bump in canary, 2) enforce CPU affinity for prefetch threads in our runtime (cheap), 3) ask infra to set scheduler knob back (might be org-level).

ryan: I can draft a tiny patch to pin prefetch threads to same CPU set as main worker (will push to perf/prefetch-affinity-fix). holds off teardown so we can validate. idea: set_thread_affinity(std::this_thread::get_id(), cpu_mask) on thread start.

maria: local test of pinned-thread patch + env fix passes. pushing a WIP PR with perf numbers.

ken: lets get the bisect results before rollback. if nvrtc is the culprit we may need vendor-eng to explain. but the pinning patch as mitigation seems safe. flag as rollout-blocker until merged.

infra-bot: created issue PERF-4123, added label: release-blocker, assigned to @maria & @ryan.

maria: opening PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/8345 — includes: thread pinning for prefetch pool + env override REDWOOD_PREFETCH_PIN=0 to disable. tests + perf bench attached.

sasha: quick review: add a comment referencing the driver/nvrtc version and link to PERF-4123. also add a note to release notes so oncall knows why we pinned.

ryan: will add tests for CPU mask env fallback. also will add a short experiment doc in /docs/ops describing the mitigation steps.

maria: thanks. gonna wait for CI perf job to confirm. if bisect proves vendor change, we'll keep pinning until vendor patch. :thumbsup: 

ci-bot: perf job (perf/bisect-prefetch-affinity) finished: 551-good, 552-bad, log: https://ci.internal/artifacts/2245678901/bisect. verdict: nvrtc/driver changes correlate strongly with regression.

ken: ok — merge pinning PR after review, push hotfix to canary, monitor. open follow-up with vendor to get a proper fix upstream.

maria: PR merged to canary, hotfix rollout started. monitoring dashboards show smallbatch median latency back within 5% of baseline. leaving PERF-4123 open for vendor tracking. :white_check_mark:
